I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1. Pacific Time (PT) is UTC-7 during standard time (not daylight saving), but in October, the U.S. is still on Daylight Saving Time (PDT), which is UTC-7.

However, in October, Spain is on Central European Summer Time (CEST), UTC+2, because Daylight Saving Time ends in Spain on the last Sunday of October — which in 2026 is October 25.

So on October 24, 2026, Madrid is still on CEST (UTC+2), and PT is still PDT (UTC-7).

The time difference between CEST (Madrid) and PDT (PT) is 9 hours: Madrid is 9 hours ahead.

Deadline: Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT.

Add 9 hours to get Madrid time:  
11:59 PM PDT + 9 hours = 8:59 AM on Saturday, October 31, 2026.

So the deadline in Madrid is 08:59 on Saturday, October 31, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 08:59
